summary: The revised target (SHA256 ce99b9a9786cd70a07e0ddcf6d86ac7b3d1b36ff1c798b824120a57651c42829) closes EOSA-001 through EOSA-005 and the P2-level EOSA-006 defects. Grok 4.6 is now mandatory review input with hash-first bounded packets, human disposition, fail-closed model pin, and tests/independent/human authority above the model. S0–S11 is mapped to Page IR, P1–P8, A0–A4, draft E0–E8, and section 10; S7–S11 are not current implementation permission. Residual P2/P3 items (pinned-model succession if x-ai/grok-4.6 is withdrawn, 22 vs claimed 25 Page IR tickets, incomplete EOS-003/015 and EOS-005/013 see-also) do not reopen a P0/P1 plan gate. Owner may accept this as planning-policy review_input only. No implementation or deployment is authorized.

findings.targetSection: §6 Verdict rules — unavailable model / no substitute
findings.issue: Unavailable-model behavior correctly fails closed with wait/stop and a narrow pre-accepted emergency rollback. There is still no lawful pin-succession path: a confirmed withdrawal of exact x-ai/grok-4.6 would block even the OS revision that could name a successor, because a different model is not a substitute and the pin-change packet would itself require x-ai/grok-4.6.

evidence.sectionOrLines: §6 Verdict rules: 'A different model or Grok version is not a substitute.'; 'Fail closed when the reported model is not exactly x-ai/grok-4.6'; 'The owner may wait or stop the affected work; there is no informal skip or substitute route.'
evidence.support: Implements the prior EOSA-001 unavailability control, but makes unpinning depend on the unavailable model.

findings.risk: Permanent process halt or shadow waiver if the pinned model is retired; does not currently block planning acceptance while the pin is available.
findings.smallestSafeCorrection: Add one owner-plus-independent-verifier pin-succession clause: if the provider confirms x-ai/grok-4.6 unavailable, freeze product work; a human-authorized OS pin-change packet may name a successor without product-implementation scope; retrospectively audit that packet with the successor model. Do not add an informal skip for ordinary tickets.

priorFindingClosure.reason: DoR/DoD now require an exact Grok 4.6 receipt, owner disposition, and no unresolved P0/P1 — not a model PASS certificate. Packets are hash-first and budgeted; identical hashes reuse receipts; reported-model mismatch and unavailability fail closed; Grok cannot close Grok P0/P1; emergency rollback is narrow; tests and humans outrank the model. Residual pin-succession is a new P2 (EOSA-007), not a reopened P0.

§6 Packet budget and data classification denies secrets, env, sites/, .one-box/, OAuth, credentials, raw uploads, browser storage, recordings, and client-identifying evidence; binaries are hash/metadata; repo artifacts are Public or Internal-Redacted; raw payloads are restricted-store with 90-day default deletion. EOS-005 now includes the external-model audit channel and audit-receipt access.

§2 splits confirmed versioned-repository inputs from time-specific live observations that are not planning-policy authority and are not used for gap severity. The 58/100 score is gone. EOS-004 is justified from the missing program backlog versus the Page IR pack and generic GitHub templates, not from unavailable git/GitHub dumps. Live 1,275-test/worktree/GitHub claims remain unavailable in this packet and are listed under evidenceMissing rather than treated as false.

§5 mapping table and grandfather rule connect S0–S11 to the program, P1–P8, A0–A4, draft E0–E8, existing OBX tickets, and section 10. S7–S11 are not in force as implementation permission. EOS-018 names the contribution-control follow-up after owner acceptance.
